## Final product and review

The final product should be checked that it meets the needs of the original request. This should be done via peer review and also checked with any main stakeholders.

More detailed quality assurance is outlined in the QA process, but products to should meet the basic criteria of providing the information required, methods assured, code reviewed, outputs checked against other appropriate data sources and produced with use the of the style guide.

Visualisations should be clear and focus on providing the insight rather than simply illustrating data. Distinction should be made between products that are made to provide information and those that are designed to provide insight.

**Information Products:** should provide clear navigation of splits of data, if used to provide comparisons, effort should be made to reduce the number of traces on a graph, to ensure columns are ordered, appropriate types of visualisations are utilised. Robust statistical methods should be used to identify trends and outliers.

**Report Products:** should focus on analysis and insight into the data. Visualisations should have purpose and be used to support insights. These reports should be kept targeted and linked to information products for further information. Report products should aim to provide recommendations and insights that led to action.

**Hybrid Products:** it is possible to do both, with a clear summary that provides an overview as well as detail that can be drilled into. This type of product is very useful, but can be challenging to get the balance right.

**Ad-hoc requests:** should focus on the insight required appropriate to the urgency and complexity of the task. Good practice should still be applied to any tables or visualisations provided and an appropriate level of QA carried out.

## Cover sheet

Analytical products should contain a cover sheet. This allows for basic metadata about the report to be found and for details such as contact information and quality assurance levels to be recorded.

An excel version of the cover sheet can obtained here : [excel cover sheet](https://nhs.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/InsightsIntelligenceteam/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B4020b094-7cb4-40a4-8115-061e07ee642d%7D&action=edit&wdenableroaming=1&wdlcid=en-GB&wdorigin=TEAMS-MAGLEV.null_ns.rwc.Sharing.DirectLink.Copy.LOF&wdexp=TEAMS-TREATMENT&wdhostclicktime=1792576631535&wdredirectionreason=Force_SingleStepBoot&wdinitialsession=2c3bfdc8-18a2-58a3-d977-70311c150b8b&wdrldsc=2&wdrldc=1&wdrldr=ContinueInExcel)

A markdown version of the cover sheet can be found here : [markdown cover sheet](https://github.com/nhsengland/sw_cover_sheet)

## SOP

Using this standard [SOP template](https://nhs.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/InsightsIntelligenceteam/Shared%20Documents/01%20-%20Analysis/10%20-%20Data%20%26%20Infrastructure/04%20-%20Reporting%20%26%20Publications/01%20-%20Product%20Catalogue/SOP%20Template%20-%20Master.docx?d=wc5adcc742e3b47ceb819ef34ccecc153&csf=1&web=1&e=e2qh2c) ensures our shared expertise, from data sources and permission paths to version control and update procedures, is clear, repeatable, and accessible to everyone.

This documentation connects directly to our [Master Product Catalogue](https://nhs.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/InsightsIntelligenceteam/Shared%20Documents/01%20-%20Analysis/10%20-%20Data%20%26%20Infrastructure/04%20-%20Reporting%20%26%20Publications/01%20-%20Product%20Catalogue/Master%20Product%20Catalogue.xlsx?d=w71133a761b3147d49904c215d94bfbcd&csf=1&web=1&e=oJ8Zbs). While the catalogue serves as the central inventory of what we deliver, each SOP provides the essential guide for how that specific output is built, refreshed, and maintained.

Each of us should take active ownership of our processes: keep your documentation fresh using our standardised naming rules, refine it as workflows evolve, and ensure the catalogue is updated with direct links to your SOPs.

Clear documentation safeguards our resilience, reduces avoidable errors, and enables every team member to step in and support one another with ease.

## Futures Workspace

The I&I Team Futures site is the front door for stakeholders to find the majority of the products and reports they will need for self-service reporting purposes. The requirements will be either:  

1.	They are already aware of a report or dashboard and need to access it regularly  

2.	They are not aware of existing dashboards but should be able to easily establish (and find) whether something exists that will suit their requirements  

Ad-hoc analyses, produced in response to a specific request, should not ordinarily be made available via Futures, unless there would be benefit in sharing the output more widely.  

Most I&I Futures pages are discoverable to anybody in the NHS with a Futures account - which means that the information contained on the pages should be accurate, clear and concise, and understandable to those who might find the page accidentally. This prevents inappropriate access requests and reduces requests for signposting / further information.   

(Note that the actual reports and dashboards have separate access permissions) 

More detail on the structure of Futures pages can be found here [Link to sharepoint Futures Instructions](https://nhs.sharepoint.com/:p:/r/sites/InsightsIntelligenceteam/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7BC3F1AFF7-AAC4-4280-97CB-1833D52492A0%7D&file=FUTURES%20Workspace%20design.pptx&action=edit&mobileredirect=true)

## Review cycle

Once a product is complete and has been signed off for production, a review date should be set with peers and stakeholders.

This should check the product is being used, is fit for purpose or requires any updates.

Reviews should be conducted at a an early stage and time between reviews extended over time as the product reaches full maturity.

This information should be documented in the product SOP under the Impact & Stakeholder Value Review section.
